findings.text: _dispatches_new_work matches any token equal to 'dispatch', 'review-plan' or 'shadow' anywhere in the command, so a continuation whose argument carries one of those words (for example a --reason value exactly 'dispatch') would have its lane stripped as if it were new work; no test pins this and the intent is the subcommand position.
the file ends without a trailing newline.

review_invocation still composes ' --local' for the review dispatch it prints (a new-work remedy), so the producer of that command still names a lane even though the obligations hook now strips it; the node correctly fenced this file as owned by a concurrent node and recorded it as a follow-on.

justifications.durability: the new behaviour is pinned red-first: tests/test_new_work_names_no_lane.py fails under the restored rewrite (negative control EXIT=1) and passes at head; is exercised in tests/test_obligations_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py through a lane-bearing redispatch. Gaps: the file has no trailing newline, and _dispatches_new_work is a whole-token membership test that would trigger a lane strip on any token equal to one of the verbs (e.g. a --reason value exactly 'dispatch'), which no test pins.
justifications.evidence: both gate logs are present and readable: gate-base.log 292 passed EXIT=0, gate-ruling.log 28 passed EXIT=0, and the manifest's five-file head arm 294 passed EXIT=0; the negative control log shows the mutation failing the new file (1 failed / 1 passed, EXIT=1) and the committed hook md5 278d0db1bb18d3c8a2eec2dd84790734 matches the worktree, so the mutation was reverted. One blemish: the after_suite names head 72a3fdb54 but the ruling gate log self-declares rev 0b09490aa (one commit short) and gate-head.log's rev header reads the base sha 494df0b11; an independent re-run of the three head files at 72a3fdb54 gave 28 passed EXIT=0, closing the gap.
justifications.fit: the edit extends the existing follow_local_lane/shlex idiom rather than introducing new machinery, the two helpers are named by mechanism (_dispatches_new_work, _without_lane), and the docstrings/comment are rewritten to the new rule. Minor: the follow_local_lane docstring says 'a lane a caller names stays the caller's to name', which reads against the fact that a composed new-work remedy's own --local is stripped.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py strips every lane flag from a dispatch/review-plan/shadow remedy and returns a continuation unchanged; a direct probe confirmed 'reckon crew dispatch ... --backend codex --local' becomes the same command with no --backend and no --local, and 'reckon crew resume --run r1 --backend codex --advice continue' is returned byte-identical. The four skill files state the same default and the plan's review_excluded_backends claim is grounded (reckon/_flight_schema.py:207).
justifications.reuse: no capability is duplicated: the lane edit lives in the hook, and the skill updates edit existing sections (routing-choice prose, command blocks) rather than adding parallel guidance; test_skill_contracts.py pins the new prose by renaming the old routing-choice test rather than adding a second overlapping one.
justifications.scope_discipline: all eleven changed paths are inside the declared write paths; the one out-of-scope concern (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:167 review_invocation still composes ' --local') is correctly left alone and reported as a follow-on rather than touched.
